label: Indonesia: reefs + rainforest · Jan 12
title: Raja Ampat, West Papua: a week diving the world's richest reefs, a week in Waigeo's rainforest
summary: 7 nights diving and snorkelling from a village homestay on Arborek, then 6 nights in Waigeo's primary rainforest (birds-of-paradise, night walks, the blue river). ~$3,460 pp.
overview:
- **What this is:** a cheaper, wilder alternative to the Africa trips, split evenly between reef and rainforest in Raja Ampat, West Papua.
- **Dates:** LAX Sat Dec 26 → LAX Tue Jan 12. 16 nights on the ground (plus 1 on a plane).
- **Route:** Jakarta 1n → Sorong 1n → **Arborek 7n** (10 dives, mantas, Piaynemo) → **Waigeo 6n** (birds-of-paradise, interior treks, night walks, Kali Biru) → Jakarta 1n.
- **Why Raja Ampat:** the Dampier Strait has the highest reef-fish and coral diversity recorded anywhere; Waigeo's interior is unlogged lowland rainforest with two birds-of-paradise found nowhere else. Few visitors, village homestays, no resorts needed.
- **Season:** October–April is the good diving season here. Expect warm showers and some wind; diving runs year-round in the strait.
- **Diving:** you're Advanced Open Water, so the Dampier Strait's current sites and deeper pinnacles (to 30 m) are open to you.
- **Budget: ~$3,460 pp**, under the $3.5k target, including ~5% contingency.

itinerary.title: Fly toward Jakarta
itinerary.details: LAX → Jakarta (CGK) with one stop in Tokyo, Taipei or Seoul, ~22–24h. ANA showed ~$1,106 round trip for December 2026 dates.

itinerary.title: Land Jakarta late
itinerary.details: Arrive CGK in the evening (the date line eats a day). Airport hotel; sleep.

itinerary.title: Fly east to Papua
itinerary.details: Morning flight CGK → Sorong (~4h; Sorong is 2h ahead of Jakarta). Afternoon in Sorong: buy cash (IDR) here — the islands have no reliable ATMs.

itinerary.title: Ferry into Raja Ampat
itinerary.details: 09:00 fast ferry Sorong → Waisai (~2h). Pay the Raja Ampat marine park tag and visitor levy at Waisai. Homestay boat to Arborek (~1h). Afternoon: snorkel the Arborek jetty — schooling fish, often wobbegong sharks under the pier.

itinerary.title: Dive day 1: check-out and Arborek reefs
itinerary.details: Two dives with Arborek Dive Shop (village-run): a check-out dive on the house reef, then a Dampier Strait site. Afternoon snorkel.

itinerary.title: Dive day 2: Cape Kri and Sardine Reef
itinerary.details: Two dives on the strait's famous current sites — Cape Kri held the record for fish species counted on one dive. Expect strong currents; the guides pick the tide. New Year's Eve in the village.

itinerary.title: Dive day 3: manta cleaning stations
itinerary.details: Two dives at Manta Sandy / Manta Ridge, where reef mantas queue at cleaning stations, plus a reef dive. Snorkellers can watch from the surface on good days.

itinerary.title: Dive day 4: Blue Magic and Mioskon
itinerary.details: Two dives on pinnacles and reefs with big schools, sharks and pygmy seahorses (ask the guide to find them). Night snorkel off the jetty if conditions allow.

itinerary.title: Dive day 5: guides' choice
itinerary.details: Last two dives of the package at the guides' pick for the conditions. Afternoon free in the water.

itinerary.title: Karst islands and lagoons
itinerary.details: Shared boat day trip west to Piaynemo: the climb to the viewpoint over the karst islands that's on every Raja Ampat poster, then snorkelling in the lagoons on the way back. A no-dive day before the forest.

itinerary.title: To the rainforest
itinerary.details: Homestay boat to Waigeo, Raja Ampat's biggest island (~1.5h). Saporkren is a village between the reef and primary lowland rainforest. Afternoon walk on the forest edge with a village guide.

itinerary.title: Birds-of-paradise at dawn
itinerary.details: Pre-dawn steep ~40-min climb to the red bird-of-paradise display tree: males dance in the canopy at first light. Afternoon by 4WD and on foot to a hide for Wilson's bird-of-paradise, found only on Waigeo and Batanta.

itinerary.title: Deep into the interior
itinerary.details: Full day on foot into unlogged lowland forest with a village guide: giant buttressed trees, hornbills crashing overhead, cockatoos and parrots, monitor lizards. After dark, a night walk for cuscus (tree-dwelling marsupials), frogs and geckos.

itinerary.title: The blue river
itinerary.details: Drive to Warsambin and trek ~1–1.5h through the forest to Kali Biru, a river of startling clear blue water in the jungle — swim in it. Forest birding on the walk back.

itinerary.title: Mangroves, reef and a second night walk
itinerary.details: Morning snorkel off Saporkren's own reef and a paddle or boat trip into the mangroves. Rest through the midday heat. Second night walk on a different trail.

itinerary.title: Last dawn in the forest
itinerary.details: Back to the display trees at dawn (better photos the second time), then a long forest hike on a new trail with your guide. Pack in the evening.

itinerary.title: Back to Jakarta
itinerary.details: Car Saporkren → Waisai (~30m), 09:00 ferry to Sorong (~2h), afternoon flight Sorong → Jakarta (~4h). Airport hotel.

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: CGK → LAX with one stop; the date line gives the day back, so you land the same calendar day. Leave 24h between your last dive (Jan 3) and flying — easily met.

booking_timeline.task: Price LAX ⇄ CGK for Dec 26 / Jan 12 (ANA, EVA, Korean, Starlux) and CGK ⇄ Sorong. Domestic schedules change often — book through the airline sites or Traveloka.
WhatsApp Arborek Dive Shop and an Arborek homestay (Stay Raja Ampat lists them) for Dec 29–Jan 5; confirm the 10-dive package, gear sizes and boat pickup from Waisai.
Book a Saporkren homestay for Jan 5–11 and its bird-of-paradise packages for Jan 6 and Jan 10; ask about guides for the interior trek and night walks.
Buy travel medical insurance with evacuation, and dive accident cover (e.g. DAN). Travel clinic: malaria prophylaxis, routine vaccines (Hep A, typhoid).
e-Visa on Arrival at evisa.imigrasi.go.id; All Indonesia arrival card within 72h of landing.
Reconfirm ferries and homestay boats; pack enough cash in IDR for the whole Raja Ampat stay (fees, homestays, diving, tips).

practical:
## Entry
- **Indonesia:** e-Visa on Arrival, IDR 500k (~$32), 30 days. Official site only: evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Passport 6+ months, 2 blank pages.
- **Raja Ampat:** marine park tag (IDR 700k) + visitor levy (IDR 1M) ≈ IDR 1.7M, cash at Waisai. Carry the tag.

## Money
- **Cash is everything.** Homestays, dive shops, boats and guides want IDR cash. Withdraw in Sorong; Waisai's ATMs are unreliable and the islands have none.

## Packing
- **No camping gear needed.** Homestays are simple huts with a mattress and mosquito net, shared bathrooms (often a bucket 'mandi'), generator power in the evening.
- Your own mask, snorkel, fins and dive computer; a rash guard; reef-safe sunscreen; a dry bag.
- Binoculars for the birds-of-paradise; a headtorch for night walks; light long sleeves and trousers against mosquitoes; trail shoes that can get wet.
- Domestic flights allow ~20 kg checked; keep dive gear light.

## Health and safety
- **Malaria:** CDC lists all of West Papua (incl. Raja Ampat) as a risk area — take prophylaxis (atovaquone-proguanil). Dengue too: DEET or picaridin day and night.
- **Diving:** strong currents in the Dampier Strait; dive with the local guides and a surface marker. Get dive accident cover — the nearest recompression chamber may be hours away.
- Medical care on the islands is minimal; evacuation cover is essential.
- Re-check the State Department's Indonesia advisory (it flags parts of the Papuan highlands, not Raja Ampat) before booking.

## Season
- Raja Ampat's diving season is roughly October–April; December–January brings showers and some northwest wind, but the Dampier Strait stays diveable.
